[untitled BTM module] These genes outline the interface between proliferative arrest and inflammatory secretion that characterises cellular senescence. On the chromatin side, the Polycomb component BMI1 is part of the complex that ubiquitinates histone H2A to silence the CDKN2A locus and keep cells cycling, while the deubiquitinase USP16 removes that mark and opposes it, so the balance between them sets how readily a cell exits the cycle.

[untitled BTM module] This grouping centres on transcriptional repression and chromatin-based silencing, the machinery that keeps developmental and proliferative genes switched off until they are needed. Polycomb components are the anchor: BMI1 is a core subunit of the PRC1 ubiquitin ligase complex that marks histone H2A to maintain silencing, while AEBP2 is a zinc-finger accessory factor that helps target the companion PRC2 methyltransferase to chromatin.

members: [untitled BTM module] This grouping describes the differentiated absorptive epithelium of the intestine and liver, the tissue that takes up nutrients, forms a selective barrier, and performs first-pass metabolism of drugs and dietary xenobiotics. Its identity is set transcriptionally by the nuclear receptors HNF4A and HNF4G, which drive expression of brush border and apical junction components such as villin, CDHR5 and the harmonin scaffold USH1C, together with the lectin LGALS4 and the tetraspanin-like TM4SF5.

[untitled BTM module] These genes define the differentiated intestinal epithelium, the absorptive lineage that lines the small bowel and colon and carries out nutrient uptake, barrier maintenance and fluid balance. The programme is set by a transcription factor core in which CDX1 and CDX2 specify intestinal identity and HNF4A and HNF4G drive enterocyte maturation; loss or ectopic activation of these factors underlies intestinal metaplasia and is used to distinguish gut-derived tumours.

[untitled BTM module] These genes mark the differentiated intestinal and hepatic epithelium and the transcriptional programme that specifies it. HNF4A and HNF4G, with FOXA3, act as master regulators of enterocyte and hepatocyte identity, driving expression of the brush-border and junctional machinery that makes an absorptive epithelium possible: villin as the microvillar actin-bundling protein, claudin-2 setting paracellular cation and water permeability in the proximal intestine, and harmonin (USH1C) organising apical scaffolds.

[untitled BTM module] These genes outline the transcriptional and structural programme that gives absorptive epithelium of the gut and kidney tubule its identity: a polarized brush-border cell that moves solutes across a sealed barrier. HNF4G, TFAP2C and SIX4 act as lineage-directing transcription factors, while CLDN2 builds a cation- and water-permeable tight junction pore that sets paracellular leakiness, and SLC3A1 supplies the heavy subunit of the transporter that reabsorbs cystine and dibasic amino acids — its loss causes cystinuria with kidney stones.

[untitled BTM module] These genes together mark the differentiated absorptive epithelium of the intestine, the cell layer that takes up nutrients, senses dietary and xenobiotic chemicals, and forms a barrier to gut contents. Lineage-defining transcription factors such as CDX1 and HNF4G impose regional intestinal identity on gut endoderm and drive expression of the enterocyte's working machinery: a brush border built with the unconventional myosin MYO1A, apical solute carriers including SLC3A1 for cystine and dibasic amino acids and the zinc transporter SLC39A5, and HMGCS2 for ketogenesis from fatty acids in a tissue with high energetic turnover.

[untitled BTM module] These genes together mark the differentiated absorptive epithelium of the intestine, the cell layer that takes up nutrients, senses dietary and xenobiotic chemicals, and forms a barrier to gut contents. Lineage-defining transcription factors such as CDX1 and HNF4G impose regional intestinal identity on gut endoderm and drive expression of the enterocyte's working machinery: a brush border built with the unconventional myosin MYO1A, apical solute carriers including SLC3A1 for cystine and dibasic amino acids and the zinc transporter SLC39A5, and HMGCS2 for ketogenesis from fatty acids in a tissue with high energetic turnover.

[untitled BTM module] This grouping describes the differentiated absorptive epithelium of the intestine and liver, the tissue that takes up nutrients, forms a selective barrier, and performs first-pass metabolism of drugs and dietary xenobiotics. Its identity is set transcriptionally by the nuclear receptors HNF4A and HNF4G, which drive expression of brush border and apical junction components such as villin, CDHR5 and the harmonin scaffold USH1C, together with the lectin LGALS4 and the tetraspanin-like TM4SF5.
only_in_confusable: [untitled BTM module] These genes mark the differentiated absorptive and secretory epithelium of the gastrointestinal tract, the barrier layer that absorbs nutrients, detoxifies luminal xenobiotics and presents a glycan-coated surface to the microbiota. Adhesion and junctional components such as EPCAM and FERMT1 hold the sheet together, while lineage transcription factors including FOXA3 and KLF5 drive and maintain the differentiated state; loss of these programmes underlies barrier failure, inflammatory bowel disease and the dedifferentiation seen in colorectal cancer, where CEACAM and galectin-4 expression is routinely used as an epithelial marker.

[untitled BTM module] The dominant theme here is chromatin-based control of gene expression coupled to ubiquitin-dependent protein regulation. Polycomb components BMI1 and EED, the histone chaperone ANP32E, the chromatin remodeller SMARCA5 and the histone-binding MORF4L2 together repress or reposition nucleosomes at developmental and proliferation genes, keeping stem and progenitor identity stable and restraining tumour suppressor loci such as the CDKN2A region.

[untitled BTM module] This grouping brings together proteins that have in common little more than a shared place in interaction screens, yet several of them converge on mitotic and genome-maintenance functions. SSNA1 is a microtubule-associated protein that promotes filament branching and localises to centrosomes and the midbody, and RASSF7 is likewise a centrosomal Ras-association domain protein required for orderly spindle formation and mitotic entry.

[untitled BTM module] This grouping centres on control of cell survival and proliferation decisions during tissue growth and differentiation. Two hubs stand out: the retinoblastoma protein RB1, which restrains the G1/S transition by holding E2F-dependent transcription in check and whose loss underlies retinoblastoma and many sporadic cancers, and BCL2L1, an anti-apoptotic member of the BCL2 family that guards mitochondrial outer membrane integrity and blocks cytochrome c release.

[untitled BTM module] This grouping centres on the housekeeping machinery that keeps mitochondria energetically competent while proteins and metabolites are turned over. Two accessory subunits of respiratory complex I sit alongside the mitochondrial translation elongation factor TUFM, which delivers aminoacyl-tRNAs to the mitoribosome and so supplies the organelle-encoded core of the respiratory chain; PRELID1 participates in phospholipid transfer between mitochondrial membranes, and TMEM160 is an inner-membrane protein.

[untitled BTM module] These genes converge on integrin-based adhesion and the cytoskeletal signalling that lets cells grip and respond to their extracellular matrix, with a supporting cast of metabolic and gene-regulatory proteins.
